# Timeline of the Anglophone Crisis (2026)

This is a timeline of the Anglophone Crisis in Cameroon during 2026.
The Anglophone Crisis is an ongoing armed conflict in the Republic of Cameroon in Central Africa, where historically English-speaking Ambazonian separatists are seeking the independence of the former British trust territory of Southern Cameroons, which was unified with Cameroon since 1961.
January
* On January 6, at least 11 separatist fighters were killed in a military ambush in Ntabah. A soldier was injured in the operation.
* On January 14, at least 14 civilians, including women and children, were killed and 14 others were injured in a suspected separatist attack in Mbandfung, Ndu.
February
* On February 8, four people were killed when armed men raided Ntumbaw, Ndu.
* On February 9, a civilian was killed during armed clashes in Bamenda.
March
* On March 6, two Cameroonian soldiers were killed in a separatist ambush in Belo.
* On March 9, a community leader from Bambui was found dead. He had been abducted by separatist fighters days prior. Previously, he had been abducted by the same group and released for ransom.
* On March 14, two separatist fighters, including a commander known as "General Jakaban", were killed in a Cameroonian raid on their hideout in Bafut. A civilian was also killed.
* On March 19, the Supreme Court of Cameroon annulled the life sentences of ten separatist leaders (the "Nera 10") from the Interim Government of Ambazonia, including Sisiku Julius Ayuk Tabe, and ordered a retrial.
* On March 28, two Cameroonian soldiers were killed and an unknown number of others were abducted in a separatist attack in Ikata, Muyuka.
April
* On April 13, three days before Pope Leo XIV’s visit to Bamenda, a separatist alliance declared a three-day ceasefire, from April 15 to 17.
* On April 22, it was reported that fresh clashes had left several soldiers and civilians dead, as separatists carried out renewed attacks following the three-day ceasefire.
* On April 26, Cameroon forces carried out a raid in Jakiri, Ndzerem-Yam raid, killing at least 14 separatist soldiers and 6 civilians. Some civilians were injured and 38 motorcycles were burned.
